The initial lift-to-drag (L/D) ratio of the rocket fins was 0.03.
The initial total radar cross-section (RCS) area of the rocket fins was -159.4 dB.
The L/D ratio was increased by 8.3 times, from 0.03 to 0.249, after optimization.
The total RCS area decreased by 12%, from -159.4 dB to -178.528 dB, after optimization.
The authors used the ANSYS adjoint solver to optimize the L/D ratio and ANSYS Optimetrics to optimize the RCS area.
The geometry was designed in CATIA and the CFD simulations were performed in ANSYS Fluent.
The CFD mesh had 427,023 elements and 140,064 nodes.
The CFD simulation used the pressure-based solver, steady-state, and the SST k-omega turbulence model, with 100 iterations.
The RCS optimization used four parameters: root chord, tip chord, leading edge, and trailing edge.
The RCS of each fin was calculated individually and then added together due to the mesh element limit.
The authors chose the optimized parameters with the lowest cost to achieve the target RCS.
The front fins had 23 possible configurations that met the target RCS, while the rear fins had 5 such configurations.
The authors used a fluid domain around the rocket geometry to perform the CFD simulations.
The primitive DATCOM approach was time-consuming and hectic, so the authors used a more efficient and user-friendly approach.
The findings of this research can be beneficial to the missile industry for developing more stealthy and efficient missiles.
